# The Lights That Guide the Lost

## Scripture

*"Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him."* — Matthew 2:2 (ESV)

## Reflection

Long before GPS or compasses, travelers looked up. The North Star held nearly still while everything else wheeled around it—a fixed point in a spinning sky. Sailors, shepherds, and wanderers oriented their whole journey by that single steady light.

But here's what's striking: the star the Magi followed wasn't a permanent fixture. It appeared, moved, and led them to a specific house in Bethlehem. God didn't just give them a general direction—He gave them a personal guide.

We often wish faith worked like the North Star: predictable, always in the same place, easy to check. Instead, God frequently leads like He led the Magi—through a light that requires us to move, to trust, to follow step by step without seeing the whole route. They didn't know where Bethlehem was. They just knew the star was worth following.

This fall, as the heavens turn overhead, remember: the God who set the stars in motion also sets His light before you. He may not show you the destination. But He promises the guidance. Sometimes the journey itself is where we learn to worship—not just when we arrive.

## Prayer

Lord, when the path ahead is unclear and I long for a fixed sign, help me trust the light You've given. Give me the Magi's courage to move when You lead, even without seeing the end. Thank You that You are not distant but guiding. In Jesus' name, amen.
